title: Ask HN: If LLM reverse engineering is deemed illegal, is that precedent for OSS?
summary:
With the efforts to clamp down on LLM-assisted reverse engineering - I am wondering;

If LLM assisted reverse engineering is deemed illegal by the courts, is that precedent for a class action that asserts OSS licenses are violated by labs that trained LLMs on that code?

There are two modalities for this;

1) LLM being post-trained against a decompiled binary - then used to output working source code.

2) LLM being used to analyze decompiled binary and used to output working source code.

How can it be "clean room" when an LLM is trained on or reads OSS but not clean room when the same is done for decompiled software?

title: Ask HN: How do you keep track of the articles, papers and videos you save?
summary:
Hi HN. This is my first post here and I would like to hear your experience on how you keep track of all the useful resources you save online. I constantly keep saving things that I find useful such as articles, papers, YouTube talks and other resources in bookmarks and open tabs (tabs are usualy reminders for me to come back to something, but I very rarely do).

More than once I ended up redoing research that I had already done because the resource I saved was burried somewhere in my bookmarks or tabs. I’m building something in this space and I would like to hear what actually works for you and how do you manage this.

What do you use today for things you want to come back to? And when you are looking for something you saved, do you actually manage to find it easily?

Also, what are some tools that you tried, but dropped eventually, and why?

I’ll post a summary of what I hear. If anyone’s up for a 20-minute call to go deeper, my email is in my profile.

title: L Coding is the new Vibe Coding
summary:
The term 'vibe-coding', to some, implies non-seriousness. It implies fickleness. It implies slop.

LLM generated code is becoming less sloppy. It is relied upon by serious and real software engineers.

I have a proposal for the new terminology.

L Code Code generated by an LLM

L Coder Someone who codes in natural language via instructions to an LLM.

L Coding The act of prompting an LLM to generate code.

heLl Code L code that has never been, and will likely never be, checked by someone who knows the language it was written in. Potentially dangerous.

title: Tell HN: HN Is Wrong
summary:
Here is a quick Show HN story.

Inspired by Alex Karpathy's HackerTube, i spent time, effort and tokens on analyzing Show HN posts - 200K plus posts, and a million plus comments, identifying trends, patterns, reactions etc.

I spent some time on designing the app too, and it felt very good because it was a 'HN community only' thing.

Then I submitted it to HN, and got zero upvotes. https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50396822. I was so sure there is some value here, that I submitted it again (from a different userid and from the same userid) but looks like the URL is banned now.

What do I do now? I have a tool that is built only for HN, it is a free tool and imo gives a set of insights based on Show HN posts, I don't have any audience anywhere so I cannot 'show' anywhere else.

The irony is this: I found the most value in the tool I built, in the 'HN is wrong' area. I find myself there now!

you can check out the tool at hackershow dot org. If you see this that is. And if someone chooses to resubmit this tool as a Show HN, please submit the 'HN is wrong' part of the tool, lets make it exciting!

Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50406993

Points: 9
